content:
I've noticed that there has been a considerable effort recently to formalize the Riemannian manifolds. E.g. with these few lines of code

import Mathlib

open Bundle CovariantDerivative

-- Base manifold
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H}
  {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  [IsManifold I 2 M]

variable [RiemannianBundle (TangentSpace I : M → _)] [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle I 1 E (TangentSpace I : M → _)]

noncomputable abbrev cov := leviCivitaConnection I M

we can define a Levi-Civita connection on a Riemannian manifold. However, I think it would be of interest to many to generalize this to pseudo-Riemannian manifolds.

The difference between the two is that RiemannianBundle assumption produces a RiemannianMetric, which is required to be positive. We could try to relax this condition, but this will not be sufficient, because the assumption is used to build the InnerProductSpace instance which also must have a positive inner operation, and this inner operation is what is used in, e.g. leviCivitaConnection to build the unique covariant derivative. In this construction on the other hand, we don't ever use the positivity.

As I see it, we could create and maintain two branches of classes, one with and one without positivity assumption (PseudoRiemannianBundle and PsuedoInnerProductSpace etc.). However I think this would be an overkill. The reason why RiemannianBundle is useful is because it links the metric to the pre-existing topology of the tangent space (via ofCoreOfTopology) which does require positivity - a link which is not needed in leviCivitaConnection for example.

The alternative would be to remove the dependency of leviCivitaConnection and friend on the RiemannianBundle and only require the user to provide the unbundled metric as a bilinear form or a linear equiv (whichever one is most general for given usecase). When the InnerProductSpace structure is present, that can alway be easily produced with InnerProductSpace.toDual.

What do you think about this? Would either of these paths would be an effort worth taking, or do you see some other solutions?

I think a good way forward would be the following:

  • introduce a class HasBilinInner (name to be chosen more wisely, probably) saying that a topological real vector space is endowed with a continuous bilinear map which is nondegenerate (or whatever is the right generality for the applications)
  • Register an instance from an inner product space to HasBilinInner
  • weaken IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle to only require that the fibers have HasBilinInner, not a full Riemannian structure. The name would have to be changed, for instance to IsContMDiffPseudoRiemannianBundle
  • Build Levi-Civita just assuming that the tangent spaces have HasBilinInner with IsContMDiffSemiRiemannianBundle.

In this way, everything should be transparent for people doing Riemannian manifolds (because Riemannian manifolds would automatically satisfy the weaker assumptions of pseudo-Riemannian manifolds).

What do you think @Michael Rothgang, @Patrick Massot, @Heather Macbeth?

If it can be helpful, there is this wip https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/pull/968
~~and https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/36299#issuecomment-4229149423~~
Edit: I have revised the physlib PR along Sébastien Gouëzel's recommendations: a fibrewise continuous symmetric nondegenerate form, with InnerProductSpace and IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle implying the weaker classes.

@Matteo Cipollina I see that your PseudoInnerProductSpace is basically exactly what @Sébastien Gouëzel suggested as HasBilinInner. I think it would be a good idea to incorporate this into Mathlib, especially that you've already done most of the work. I would maybe generalize this to a [CommSemiring 𝕜] [StarRing 𝕜] rather than specialize to real numbers only, and make the map sesquilinear?
Pseudo? Certainly O'Neill uses the term Semi-Riemannian. I don't particularly care though.
